newsitem.title: USA: Site of environmental disaster to become park.
newsitem.headline: Site of environmental disaster to become park.

text.p: Times Beach, the Missouri village of 2,300 abandoned and leveled because of dioxin contamination, will be turned into a state park, officials announced Wednesday.

The 524-acre site along the Meramec River southeast of St. Louis will become a park dedicated to U.S. Route 66, the Chicago-to-Los Angeles highway that was a major east-west link until the 1950s when the Interstate highway system covered parts of it and bypassed the rest.

The Missouri Department of Natural Resources, which made the announcement, said the park will contain a museum devoted to Route 66, which once ran nearby, as well as a display telling the story of Times Beach.

Times Beach was evacuated and leveled after a waste hauler dumped industrial oil contaminated with dioxin on the town's dirt streets to hold down dust. The town's alderman voted in 1985 to dissolve the abandoned village.
About 265,000 tons of dioxin-tainted soil and debris were burned in an incinerator in a clean-up that ended last month. Dioxin is a chemical contaminant linked to health problems, including cancer.
The area was to be graded and re-planted before the park opens.
